Sources: crates.io rama-boring 0.7.0 and rama-boring-sys 0.7.0.
Upstream: https://github.com/plabayo/rama-boring
The original package license files and BoringSSL source licenses are retained.

Kerlico changes:
- rama-boring/src/ssl/connection.rs adds two ClientHelloShape switches.
- rama-boring-sys/build/main.rs applies kerlico_legacy_extensions.patch after the upstream patches.
- kerlico_legacy_extensions.patch controls initial EMS and renegotiation_info emission inside the TLS engine.
- kerlico_profile_wire.patch preserves an explicitly ordered padding extension and known key shares requested by an explicit Preserve profile. PSK remains last.
- rama-boring/src/ssl/quic.rs exposes SSL_quic_read_level through the existing EncryptionLevel enum for Quinn integration.
- Existing SSL_key_update and zero-length SSL_write are exposed as safe Rust request_key_update/flush_tls methods so read-only TLS streams can acknowledge control messages.
- Existing SSL_set1_tls_channel_id is exposed as a safe Rust setter for the old 360 profile.
- Existing X509_sign with its documented null digest is exposed as sign_without_digest for Ed25519 certificate issuers.
- QUIC ChromeParrot fields follow apernet/quic-go 184d081eef3e chromeQUICClientHelloSpec; captured UQUICClient output was compared with native output.

Approved by the user on 2026-11-09 for exact Xray ClientHello fingerprints.
Application logic remains Rust. The patch does not modify certificate verification,
rewrite BIO bytes, enable renegotiation, or depend on private structure offsets.
Builds use these pinned local packages without a Git download.
